rationale: The baseline oscillates badly: non-harmonic content is -5.3 dB, loop-break phase margin is 17.5 deg at a 1.91 MHz UGF, and closed-loop peaking is 9.1 dB. The likely cause is the buffer/gate pole of the large-Ciss output devices, driven through Rk/RS/Rup of about 47-150 ohm, sitting near the UGF. Raising CC from 10 pF to 22 pF should cut the Miller-set UGF to about 0.85 MHz without adding any bias power, which should increase phase margin. r1 and rf are snapped to E24 (5.1k, 910k), so beta goes to 0.195 and the gain to about 4.14, which keeps the HD-test output near 2.07 Vpk. Only CC changes the circuit in a meaningful way, so this run shows how f3db_ol (follower method) responds to compensation. That reading looks inflated or distorted by the peaking: its implied GBW of about 9 MHz is far above the 1.9 MHz loop-break UGF.
expected_effect: P_avg should stay about the same (~0.74 W) because the bias network is untouched. Stability should improve: PM about 40-55 deg, less closed-loop peaking, and non-harmonic content hopefully below -30 dB. std_values should pass. HD and swing should stay about -35 dBc and 2.1/2.5 Vpk. f3db_ol (follower) is uncertain and could drop if the measurement tracks the true GBW; that would tell us the bandwidth constraint needs a higher buffer pole (lower Rk/RS) rather than less compensation.

rationale: At k=1 the phase margin was 32 deg with a 1.7 MHz UGF, and the likely second pole is at the output-device gates. Roughly 2-3 nF of effective gate capacitance (Ciss plus Miller-multiplied Cgd) sees Rup||(RS + 1/gm_2N7000||Rk), about 150||(47+15) = 44 ohm, which puts a pole near 1.4 MHz. I am scaling the gate-drive network down: Rup 150->100, RS 47->30, Rk 47->22. That gives about 100||(30+7) = 27 ohm at VQ2 and about 7 ohm at VQ1, moving the buffer pole out by about 1.6-2x. The gate-to-gate offset stays near 0.87 V (k=1: 19.3 mA x 47 = 0.91 V), so the class-AB quiescent current should stay the same or drop slightly. I am holding CC (22 pF), the tail and Rf/Rin fixed to isolate this one effect. I am not taking the critic's Rf 680k suggestion: a larger beta raises the crossover frequency and would lower the phase margin further.
expected_effect: Expected: phase margin rises above about 45 deg, nonharm drops below -30 dB and closed-loop peaking falls well below 24.5 dB. P_avg rises by about 0.12-0.14 W because I_VCC1 goes from about 27 mA to about 55 mA (Rup about 29 mA, 2N7000 about 26 mA). VCC2 quiescent should be about the same or slightly lower. Ratings stay inside limits: P_Rup about 84 mW, P_Rk about 65 mW, 2N7000 about 0.1 W. f3db_ol (follower) will still fail at about 87 kHz because CC is unchanged. If stability passes, the next step is to cut CC toward 10 pF or below to recover bandwidth, and then cut bias power.
